transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve gotten myself in a bit over my head. I took on this historical society fundraiser and started acting like I could run the whole thing myself—quilt designs, calling volunteers, schedules, deadlines. I promised more than I could really manage.
During this time, have you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable compared with your normal self?
Yes… I suppose I did. At first I felt kind of… bright, almost glowing, like every idea I had was a good one. But if someone questioned me, I’d get snappish. Like they were in my way.
During that time, did you need less sleep than usual?

Yes. I wasn’t sleeping much—just a few hours, and then I’d wake up feeling like I should get straight to sewing or making calls. Lately it’s sort of gone the other way… I’m either awake worrying, or I sleep late and still feel tired.
During that time, were you more active or driven to get things done than is usual for you?

Yes. I was… constantly up doing something. I couldn’t even sit through a TV show with my husband without jumping up to measure fabric, write things down, move supplies around. It felt like I had to keep going.
During that time, did you feel more capable or important than usual?
Yes… I did. I don’t know, it sounds silly now, but I really thought my quilt ideas were going to make people notice our town. Like I’d found something only I could do.
During that period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life or responsibilities?

Yes… it did. My husband’s had to pick up a lot of the household things I usually handle. And with the historical society… I stopped keeping up with what I’d promised, and then I couldn’t really face the people waiting on me.
During that time, were you talking more than usual or so much that other people had trouble interrupting you?
Yes… I guess I was. In meetings I’d get going about the patterns, the budget, publicity… and I’d talk so fast people would try to cut in, but I just kept talking. It felt hard to stop.
During that bright, energized time, did you have any experiences like hearing voices or becoming convinced of something others said wasn’t true?

I… don’t think so. I was very caught up in my ideas, but I don’t remember hearing voices or anything like that. As for being convinced of things… I’m not sure. I thought my plans made sense at the time.
About how many days did that bright, energized period last?
It was… longer than a few days. About five months, I think, before it all kind of came apart.
